transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah. I guess I’m here because I’ve been kind of hard on myself lately. At work I keep feeling like I’m not really senior-level material, like maybe I somehow convinced people I can handle more than I actually can. 

I know that might sound a little dramatic, but it’s been on my mind enough that I thought I should probably talk to someone about it.
Have you been feeling down or hopeless about yourself or your abilities more often than not, especially outside of work situations?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but most days lately there’s been this kind of heavy, low feeling. Not just at work, really. It’s like I’m getting through work and then home too, but everything feels sort of… muted, like the color’s turned down. If that makes sense.
Have you found that you don’t take as much pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or even time with friends or family?

Yeah… a bit, I guess. I mean, I still like those things in theory, you know? Usually I look forward to grilling on the weekend, or going fishing, or just putting on a record and relaxing.

Lately, though, I kind of just… don’t. The grill stuff sits there, the fishing gear sits there, even the records. I’ll think about doing it and then it just feels like too much effort, or like I don’t really care enough to start. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you noticed that you've been feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you haven't been doing much?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I’m still getting through the day, so I don’t want to overstate it, but by the time I get home from the office, even simple stuff feels like a lot more effort than it should. Like checking the mail, or loading the dishwasher… things that shouldn’t really be a big deal.

Is that the kind of tired you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I wouldn’t say it’s dramatic or anything, but my appetite’s been kind of off. Some nights I’ll just grab a few bites of something, or skip supper because nothing really sounds worth making.

And… my belt does feel a little looser lately, but I haven’t been trying to lose weight. I’m not sure how much, though. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just in specific situations like work?

Yeah… I think that’s fair. I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly, or maybe I just don’t like saying it that way, but most days lately there’s this kind of heavy, low feeling.

It’s not only work, really. I’ll be at the office or at home and I’m just sort of moving through things, like everything’s got the color turned down a little. Does that make sense?

Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or even time with friends or family, not just that they feel like more effort, but that you don’t care about them anymore?

Not completely, I guess… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But yeah, the stuff I usually look forward to just doesn’t pull me in lately.

Like, normally I’d be thinking about grilling on the weekend, or maybe going fishing, or even just putting on a record after work. Lately the grill stuff just sits there, the fishing gear sits there, and I don’t really feel much about it. It’s not even that I’m too busy… I just kind of don’t care enough to start.

Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual, or that it's harder to get yourself going, even when you know you need to do something?

Yeah… maybe not moving slowly exactly, at least I don’t think anyone would notice, but I do feel kind of… worn down.

By the time I get home from the office, even little things like checking the mail or loading the dishwasher feel like more effort than they really should. I still usually make myself do them, or at least some of them, but it takes more pushing than it used to. Does that count?
Have you been feeling this way — with a low or heavy mood — nearly every day for the past two weeks or more?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but most days lately it’s been there — that heavy, low kind of feeling. Like I’m getting through work and home and everything, but it all feels a bit dulled down, if that makes sense.
Have you found that nothing really brings you pleasure or satisfaction anymore, even things you used to really enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say absolutely nothing, maybe that sounds too strong. But the things I usually enjoy just don’t really do much for me lately.

Like, I normally look forward to grilling on the weekend, or going fishing, or just putting on a record. And lately I just kind of leave the grill stuff or fishing gear sitting there. I see it, and I know I usually like it, but I don’t really care enough to do it. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?

Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in *everything* you used to enjoy — like hobbies, activities, or even time with friends or family — not just that they feel like more effort, but that you don’t care about them anymore?

I don’t know if I’d say completely everything… that sounds pretty extreme, and I’m still around people and all that.

But, yeah, the stuff I usually look forward to — grilling on the weekend, fishing, putting on a record — lately I just kind of leave it sitting there. I’ll see the grill stuff or the fishing gear and think, “I normally like that,” but I don’t really feel much pull to do it. It’s not just effort, I guess… it’s more like I don’t care about it the way I usually do. Does that make sense?
Would you say that your low energy or tiredness has been present most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks or more?

Yeah… I think so, most days. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is — I’m still getting through work and everything — but by the time I get home from the office, even little things feel like a lot.

Like checking the mail or loading the dishwasher… stuff that should be nothing, really, just feels like it takes more effort than it ought to. Does that count as what you mean by low energy?

Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in almost all activities — things you used to enjoy, or even things you normally have to do — not just that they feel like more effort, but that you don’t care about them anymore?

I don’t know if I’d say completely, because that sounds like… a lot. But yeah, the main things I usually enjoy, they just don’t have the same pull.

Like I normally look forward to grilling on the weekend, or going fishing, or just putting on a record, and lately I’ll see the stuff sitting there and I just kind of leave it. I don’t really care enough to start. It’s not that I hate those things now, I just… don’t feel much about them right now, if that answers it.

Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in almost all activities — things you used to enjoy, or even things you normally have to do — not just that they feel like more effort, but that you don’t care about them anymore?

I mean… I wouldn’t say completely, because I don’t want to overstate it. But yeah, with the things I normally like — grilling on the weekend, fishing, putting on a record — lately I just kind of leave the stuff sitting there.

It’s like I know I usually care about it, but right now I don’t really feel that pull to do it. I don’t know if that’s what you mean, but… yeah, I guess I don’t care about those things the way I normally do.

Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest and pleasure in *all* activities — things you used to enjoy, and even things you normally have to do — not just that they feel like more effort, but that you don’t care about them or get any enjoyment from them anymore?

I don’t know if I’d say all activities, or completely… I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.

But the usual stuff I look forward to — grilling on the weekend, fishing, putting on a record — lately I’ll see it there and just sort of leave it. I don’t really feel much pull toward it, or care enough to start. So… yeah, I’m not getting the same enjoyment from those things, if that’s what you mean.

Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest and pleasure in almost all activities — things you used to enjoy and even things you normally have to do — not just that they feel like more effort, but that you don’t care about them or get any enjoyment from them anymore?

I think… almost all might be a little strong, maybe. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But the stuff I normally do look forward to — grilling on the weekend, fishing, even just putting on a record — lately I’ll see it there and I just kind of leave it. I don’t really feel that interested, or like I care enough to start. So yeah, I’m not getting much enjoyment out of those things right now, if that makes sense.

Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest and pleasure in almost all activities — things you used to enjoy and even things you normally have to do — not just that they feel like more effort, but that you don’t care about them or get any enjoyment from them anymore?

I guess… not completely, or at least I don’t want to say it that strongly if that’s not accurate.

But yeah, the things I usually do enjoy — like grilling on the weekend, going fishing, putting on a record — lately I’ll just see the stuff sitting there and I don’t really feel like doing it. It’s not even just effort, it’s more like I don’t care enough to start, which isn’t really like me. Does that answer what you’re asking?

Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities — things you used to enjoy and even things you normally have to do — not just that they feel like more effort, but that you genuinely don’t care about them or get any enjoyment from them anymore?

I mean… yeah, I guess that’s closer to it. I don’t want to say I get nothing from anything, because that sounds pretty extreme.

But the things I usually look forward to — grilling on the weekend, fishing, putting on a record — lately I just kind of leave the stuff sitting there. It’s not just that it feels like work. I just don’t really care enough to do it, or I don’t expect to enjoy it much. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
